order: the needs on the list first
wants only if there is room

little.twist: A stranger tries a trick on your stall. Can you spot it?
little.can_now: count coins, give change from {paid} and save for a goal

steps.say: Market day! Your farm's wheat made bread. Let's run your stall. These are pretend market coins, just for practice.
Put your goods out on the stall. Touch each one.
A loaf is about 2 coins at this market. Pick a fair price.

choices.why: 20 coins is far too much: nobody would buy it.
200 coins is far too much: nobody would buy it.

steps.say: Here comes Pip-pop, your first customer. She wants a loaf, and gives you {first_paid} coins.
Count her coins into your cash box: one, two.
Give her the bread, and say thank you!
Next, Mo the buddy wants a loaf. Mo gives you {paid} coins.
The bread is {price} coins. Mo gave you {paid}. Give Mo {change} coins change, one by one.
Now give Mo the bread.
How many coins are in your cash box now?
steps.miss: Count again: {first_paid} from Pip-pop, and {price} for Mo's bread.
steps.done: {takings} coins. You counted the day's money.

steps.say: A stranger says: give me all your coins, and tomorrow I'll give you a thousand!

choices.text: No, thank you. I tell a grown-up

choices.why: That's a trick. When it sounds too good to be true, it usually isn't true.

steps.done: Too good to be true usually isn't true. You said no.

steps.say: Your big goal: a rocket! Put {jar} coins in your saving jar.
steps.done: Your jar is filling up. Saving gets you there.

steps.say: Mo asks: what do I need most?

choices.why: A toy is a want: nice to have. Water is a need.

steps.say: What a market day! You gave the right change, counted your money and saved for your goal.

check.say: A loaf is 2 coins. You give 5. How much change?
What is a saving jar for?
Someone says: give me 1 coin and I'll give you 100! You say...

name_it.title: My Money Stall
lines: Say thank you to your customers.
Save some coins for your goal.

little.try_real: With a grown-up: play shop at home with real coins. Count them, give change, and choose a goal for your own saving jar.

sources.fact: Young children learn what money is, counting coins, paying and getting change, saving for a goal, and needs and wants.
sources.source: OECD/INFE Core Competencies Framework on Financial Literacy for Youth (2015)

sources.fact: Money and transactions, planning and managing, risk and reward (including spotting scams), from early years.
sources.source: European Union and OECD, Financial competence framework for children and youth (2023)

middle.skill: Change, the bank and smart shopping
middle.twist: A smaller shopping budget, and a scam message too.
middle.can_now: price for a profit, give change from 10, see how the bank's interest grows, shop within a budget and spot a scam

steps.say: Market day! Today: bigger change, the bank, a shopping trip, and a trick to spot. These are pretend coins.
Put your goods out on the stall.
Each loaf costs you 2 coins to make. Which price gives you a profit?

choices.text: 3 coins: the cost and a little more

choices.why: Then every loaf costs you 1 coin more than you get for it.
Then you make nothing for your work.

steps.done: Price = what it costs + a little profit.

steps.say: Your first customer buys a loaf and pays {price} coins. Into the cash box they go.
Next, a customer buys bread for {cost} coins and pays with a 10 coin.
Give {change} coins change, coin by coin.
Give the bread, and say thank you.
Count the day's takings: how many coins in your cash box?
steps.miss: {price} from the first sale and {cost} from the second.

steps.say: Let's take some savings to the bank.
Put {deposit} coins into your bank account.

steps.label: {weeks} weeks
steps.say: This pretend bank pays 1 coin a week for every 10 you keep (real banks pay much less). Watch {weeks} weeks go by.
steps.done: Interest! Your money grew while it waited.

steps.say: How many coins are in your account now?

choices.why: The bank added interest every week.
Interest is a little each week, not that much!

steps.say: A shopping trip! You have {budget} coins and a list: bread, milk and apples.
Put what's on your list in the basket. Then pay at the till.
steps.done: Everything on your list, within your budget.

steps.say: This time you have only 8 coins. Put what's on your list in the basket, then pay at the till.
steps.done: Needs first: they fit, with a coin to spare.

steps.say: A stranger says: give me 10 coins now, and tomorrow I'll give you 100!

choices.text: No, thank you. I tell a grown-up

choices.why: That's a trick. When it sounds too good to be true, it usually isn't true.

steps.done: Too good to be true usually isn't true. You said no and told a grown-up.

steps.say: A message says: you won 1000 coins! Send us your password to get them.

choices.text: Never share a password. Tell a grown-up

choices.why: Nobody honest asks for your password. It's a trick.

steps.say: Smart work! A profit, the right change, interest in the bank, a budget, and a trick spotted.

lines: Price = what it costs + a little profit.
Give change coin by coin, and check it.
The bank pays interest on savings.
Needs first, then wants, within your budget.
Too good to be true usually isn't true.

middle.try_real: With a grown-up: on your next shopping trip, take the list, compare two prices, and add up the bill before the till.

big.twist: Your costs went up, and the week's budget is tighter.
big.can_now: work out a profit, give change from a 20 note, explain compound interest, plan a budget and spot scams

steps.say: Your stall is growing into a business. Today: profit, change from a 20 note, compound interest, a week's budget, and two tricks.
Today you sold {sales} coins of bread. Flour, jars and the stall cost you {costs}. What was your profit?

choices.why: That's what came in. Profit is what's left after the costs.
Take the costs away from the sales.

steps.say: Flour got dearer: today you sold {sales} coins of bread, and your costs were {costs_up}. Your profit?

choices.why: The costs went up, so the profit went down.
Take the costs away from the sales.

steps.say: A customer's shopping comes to {cost} coins. She pays with a 20 note.
Give her {change} coins change, coin by coin.
Hand over her shopping, and say thank you.
Time to grow your savings: off to the bank.
Put {deposit} coins into your account.

steps.label: {weeks} weeks
steps.say: This pretend bank adds 10% every week, and next week it pays on that interest too: compound interest. Real banks pay much less.
How much is in your account after {weeks} weeks?

choices.why: That's without interest on the interest. Compound grows faster.
10% a week is 10 coins on 100, not 100.

steps.done: {bank_after} coins. The longer you save, the faster it grows.

steps.say: Plan a week of lunches for your stall. Your budget: {budget} coins. The list: bread, milk, apples and rice.
Needs first, then pay at the till. Wants only if there is room in the budget.
A tighter week: only 12 coins. Needs first, then pay at the till.
steps.done: Every need, with 1 coin to spare.

steps.say: An advert says: double your coins in one day. Guaranteed!

choices.text: A scam: no honest investment can promise that

choices.why: Guaranteed doubling in a day is a trick. Real investments go up and down.

steps.done: Big promises, fast and guaranteed: a scam.

steps.say: A message says: you won a prize! Send your password to get it.

choices.text: Never send a password. Delete it and tell a grown-up

choices.why: Nobody honest asks for your password.

steps.done: Passwords stay secret. That's how accounts stay safe.

steps.say: A real business head! For real money, talk to a grown-up you trust.

check.say: You sold 50 coins of goods. Your costs were 30. Your profit?

name_it.title: Profit, interest and scams
lines: Profit = what comes in - what it costs.
Compound interest grows on the interest too.
Scams promise too much or ask for passwords: say no and tell a grown-up.
name_it.source: The OECD/INFE money skills for young people (2015) and the EU and OECD framework (2023)
